variantDescriptions.weak: probe build `cc4d21fd8d` (`scala2-perf-integration` `6101d220ca` + counters), uniques in the usual `WeakHashSet`; per-run counters in `jmh.log` (`[uniques] ...`)
variantDescriptions.strong: the same build with `-Dscalac.uniques.strong=true`: unique types held strongly for the run, so GC never clears them

name: m5-forkvar-uniques
description: Does GC clearing of the weak `uniques` table make the compiler's work vary from fork to fork? Probe branch `claude/forkvar-uniques-probe`. Compare the spread of instructions/op between `weak` and `strong`, and the mean (what clearing costs). Each run prints lookups, additions and GC-cleared entries to `jmh.log`; their spread across forks says how much the table churns. Locally (typer on `Types.scala` and `tpe/`), weak runs added 0–1.4% more types depending on GC, strong runs were identical.

Local copy of `m4-forkvar-uniques` on the M5 Pro laptop while the m4 is unreachable: read instructions/op and the `[uniques]` counters, not time (the laptop's endpoint security moves cycles at equal instructions). Load gate loosened to 3 cores for the same reason.
